review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is supported because neither a qualifying ending nor positive current operation is established. Statutory repeal and agency termination remain candidates under the supplied rules. Approval of a regulatory code cannot be assumed to have exhausted its operative effect merely because the approval sentence is self-executing; the approved code's terms remain unexamined. Formal status is supported only as the limited finding that no express ending was found in the reviewed evidence.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (NOT_FOUND fits the unresolved first ending, consistent with FIRST_END_UNRESOLVED in the evidence slice; WEB fits the specifically identified missing code text). The supplied rules already prohibit treating an unnamed general statute as a proven ending. No evidence establishes that an owner ruling is the necessary missing item.

verdicts.reason: Both held texts confirm code approval and adoption of the Administrator's report, recommendations and findings; the clause inventory includes both actions.
The second held text contains the approval sentence, [No. 6331-B], and the U.S. Government Printing Office 1933 imprint.
The first held text expressly invokes NIRA Title I, with the additional words 'and otherwise'.

49 Stat. 375, section 2, confirms the quoted repeal of code-approval and enforcement provisions. Verified at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-49/pdf/STATUTE-49-Pg375.pdf. It does not name EO 6331-B.
Section 1 of the same official page confirms substitution of April 1, 1936, in NIRA section 2(c). This supports the statutory sunset candidate, not an independently established ending of this order.

The cited U.S. Code page identifies sections 703 and 712 as omitted and contains the quoted Schechter passage. Its text is current through October 9, 2026; it does not affirm this order's continuing operation.
The cited Code page reproduces EO 7252 section 2 and the quoted termination direction for agencies transferred to Commerce. It does not name EO 6331-B.
